scope: Red team of a portable executable domain-package boundary, not a denial that useful executable rules exist.
verdict: Do not infer a product opportunity from the existence of reusable rules. Require incremental value over native tools and project-local automation.
kills_thesis_semantics: Conditional impact if the stated rejection condition is established for the preregistered claim and workload. yes is not a finding that the condition has already occurred; partially rejects a stronger claim or a component of it; no would leave the claim intact.
severity_semantics: critical threatens safety or the proposed product boundary; high materially threatens feasibility, scope or adoption. Priority is an argued investigation order, not a measured probability.

risks.title: No amortization before the workload changes
risks.critique: Encoding saves repeated reasoning only if reuse pays for extraction, adapters, updates, review, support and residual failures within a buyer's actual horizon.
risks.evidence_limit: The sources establish a conditional economic principle and concrete lifecycle or review obligations, not measured MEDP costs or negative ROI.
risks.impact: A technically reusable package can be a more expensive way to deliver the same migrations.
risks.mitigation: Choose frequent stable workloads and automate package production.
risks.mitigation_failure: Selection after observing failure is circular; model-generated packages still need independent review and ongoing ownership.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Architecture cannot create reuse demand or remove the opportunity cost of expert review.
risks.kill_scope: Economic viability of this package product in the preregistered segment and horizon.
risks.rejection_condition: Even the optimistic credible incremental savings bound is nonpositive at the buyer's realistic reuse volume and safety requirements.

risks.title: Incumbent artifacts already capture the useful knowledge
risks.critique: Versioned recipes, policy bundles, native validators and a thin adapter may provide all useful behavior without a new cross-domain package contract.
risks.evidence_limit: Documented native capabilities do not establish their combined runtime equivalence to the proposed system.
risks.impact: The proposal risks paying a translation and governance tax to duplicate established ecosystems; agent access alone is not differentiation.
risks.mitigation: Position the new format as a unifying composition contract.
risks.mitigation_failure: A wrapper that renames native fields without improving integration cost, enforcement or portability does not justify a standard.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Architectural elegance cannot establish incremental customer value.
risks.kill_scope: Need for a new shared package layer, not native executable knowledge.
risks.rejection_condition: Native composition or project-local automation meets the same predeclared quality, authority and audit requirements at lower total cost, with no valued portability advantage.

risks.title: Target semantics change what must be observed
risks.critique: A neutral assessment can omit the business and runtime facts needed to evaluate a target. Provider selection can require new observations, not merely a different rule over fixed facts.
risks.evidence_limit: Messaging documentation provides a counterexample to simplistic neutral fields, not a test of the proposed .NET hosting prototype or proof that all shared observations are impossible.
risks.impact: Scan-once neutrality may become a lossy lowest common denominator or an ever-growing union of target-specific facts.
risks.mitigation: Represent capabilities richly and allow target packages to request further observations.
risks.mitigation_failure: This can be technically sound, but concedes one fixed neutral assessment and adds provider-dependent acquisition cost; encode everything is not a finite completeness argument.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: A representation cannot infer an unobserved business invariant; a staged observation protocol narrows rather than proves the original promise.
risks.kill_scope: Strong scan-once and clean late-stage provider-separation claims.
risks.rejection_condition: A supported target needs facts absent from the frozen shared observation contract, or a supposedly portable rule requires target-specific behavior inside the neutral core.

risks.title: Deterministic validation can repeat the same wrong assumption
risks.critique: A transform and its tests can share a mistaken model of intended behavior. Reproducibility does not make the decision correct, and distributing the same bad rule can correlate failures across customers.
risks.evidence_limit: Alembic and Cargo document bounded detection and review needs; correlated fleet losses are a risk model, not a measured incident rate for domain packages.
risks.impact: False confidence can convert one expert mistake into many identical damaging changes; a low average defect rate can hide unacceptable tail loss.
risks.mitigation: Add independent behavioral tests, canaries, explicit assumptions and human approvals.
risks.mitigation_failure: These controls cost money, cannot validate unspecified intent, and may reduce autonomy or require production-like state and accountable owners.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: The correctness oracle and acceptable loss are external domain obligations, not consequences of a schema.
risks.kill_scope: Safety claims based on typed legality or deterministic checks alone; possibly economics if adequate safeguards erase savings.
risks.rejection_condition: The system authorizes a seeded damaging transformation despite its claimed sufficient checks, or independent safety controls erase the economic advantage.

risks.title: An authoritative package cannot police its client
risks.critique: If an agent can edit the input, replace the validator or execute changes outside the gate, immutable package contents do not prevent quiet redefinition of the effective domain.
risks.evidence_limit: The repository assigns approvals and execution to a harness; no bypass-resistant implementation was tested in WS-04.
risks.impact: The central authority guarantee actually depends on privilege boundaries, trusted observations and complete mediation of execution.
risks.mitigation: Use an independently administered execution gate with constrained credentials and authenticated evidence.
risks.mitigation_failure: This is a legitimate control, but creates a security/control-plane product and associated operations; it is not a property of the package format.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: A library cannot restrict a more-privileged caller. Assigning enforcement to the same unconstrained agent is circular.
risks.kill_scope: Package-level authority independent of a trusted harness; not the usefulness of publishing rules separately.
risks.rejection_condition: Any in-scope client can carry out a denied action or substitute evidence without a separately authorized override and a durable record.

risks.title: Trustworthy origin is not trustworthy expertise
risks.critique: Executable domain packages import dependency compromise and authorized-but-wrong producer risks into consequential decision making.
risks.evidence_limit: The xz disclosure is a real upstream compromise, not an observed domain-package attack or proof that signatures are useless. SLSA addresses many tampering threats but excludes malicious-producer correctness.
risks.impact: Signing or pinning a package can preserve and distribute a bad decision; revocation, replacement, offline availability and liability still need owners.
risks.mitigation: Pin transitive inputs, verify attestations, restrict privileges, review high-impact rules and provide revocation and rollback.
risks.mitigation_failure: These reduce specific threats but add operating costs and cannot make a trusted author's business judgment correct; a lock may not cover every dependency class.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Producer trust and organizational acceptance of risk cannot be derived solely from producer-issued metadata.
risks.kill_scope: Claims that origin verification is sufficient trust or that governance is nearly free.
risks.rejection_condition: A correctly attributed but deliberately incorrect test package receives automatic authority, or revocation cannot stop subsequent consequential use within the declared deadline.

risks.title: Compatibility is a relation, not a version number
risks.critique: Engine, framework, provider, policy, schema and application-state combinations multiply the compatibility surface; independently valid packages need not compose safely.
risks.evidence_limit: Kubernetes skew rules establish coupled compatibility; any proposed Cartesian product is illustrative, not a measured MEDP test requirement.
risks.impact: Certification can consume the savings from portability, or unsupported combinations can quietly become runtime experiments.
risks.mitigation: Declare supported profiles, lock versions, use pairwise testing and refuse unknown combinations.
risks.mitigation_failure: Pairwise coverage does not prove higher-order interactions; refusing combinations is safe but shrinks addressable reuse. Calling only successful clients compatible after the fact is circular.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: A manifest can describe a support boundary but cannot establish its truth without evidence.
risks.kill_scope: Broad interchangeability independent of a bounded compatibility matrix.
risks.rejection_condition: Previously declared supported combinations diverge or require per-client rule forks, or the measured supported-profile cost exceeds its reuse value.

risks.title: Knowledge ownership becomes a permanent service obligation
risks.critique: The valuable rules may be precisely those that require continued expert attention as platforms, safety constraints and customer exceptions evolve.
risks.evidence_limit: Documented lifecycle limits and support scopes demonstrate maintenance obligations, not their cost or a community's willingness to fund them.
risks.impact: A package registry can externalize support work to unpaid maintainers or turn into a bespoke consulting operation.
risks.mitigation: Fund maintainers, narrow scope and provide automated compatibility tests.
risks.mitigation_failure: Funding needs recurring customer value; automating tests does not determine evolving intended behavior or resolve absent maintainers.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Accountable ownership and sustainable incentives are not serialization problems.
risks.rejection_condition: No owner can meet the predeclared update/support budget, or two update cycles require enough exception work to eliminate projected savings.

risks.title: The model-assisted alternative improves during payback
risks.critique: A package justified by today's expensive reasoning may become stranded investment if cheaper or better models plus native tools solve the same work before payback.
risks.evidence_limit: Stanford reports a historical over-280-fold inference cost decline at GPT-3.5-level performance, not migration cost. METR's early-2025 slowdown is historical; its 2026 follow-up warns of unreliable effect-size estimates from selection and timing problems.
risks.impact: A static model baseline can overstate durable savings. Conversely, cheaper inference can also reduce package authoring cost and improve its client.
risks.mitigation: Target costly failures rather than tokens, and use improved models to maintain the package.
risks.mitigation_failure: The same improvement benefits competitors; authoring savings do not imply review savings. Neither model progress nor failure avoidance can be assumed from benchmark scores.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Relative economic performance over time must be measured and stress-tested, not guaranteed by decomposition.
risks.kill_scope: The claimed durable cost advantage in the chosen segment and horizon.
risks.rejection_condition: A current or preregistered sensitivity-case native/model baseline matches required quality and beats the package's full cost before its payback horizon; sensitivity results alone are conditional, not observed rejection.

risks.title: Rule priority cannot resolve conflicting obligations
risks.critique: Community advice, provider constraints, organization policy and user intent are not interchangeable authority levels. Deterministic precedence can consistently select an impermissible outcome or hide an unsatisfiable request.
risks.evidence_limit: The prototype names separate rule owners and Helm documents unresolved lifecycle governance. The conflicting-policy examples in the analysis are constructed, not observed customer disputes.
risks.impact: A technically legal transition can violate an independent obligation; escalation and exceptions can dominate workflow latency.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit prohibitions, unsatisfiable outcomes, named exception authorities and expiring overrides.
risks.mitigation_failure: A solver can report inconsistency but cannot decide which organization is entitled to waive which obligation. Always asking a human may erase automation value.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Legitimate authority and substantive agreement must exist outside the resolver.
risks.kill_scope: Automatic useful composition of independently owned rules without costly governance.
risks.rejection_condition: Contradictory hard constraints produce an executable plan, or valid resolution requires unbudgeted case-by-case negotiation.

risks.title: Provenance may be an expense buyers will not fund
risks.critique: Lineage can improve debugging and accountability without supporting a separate buying decision; complete replay also competes with privacy, storage and operational limits.
risks.evidence_limit: OPA documents useful decision logs and explicit masking/dropping limits. There is no observed willingness-to-pay evidence for this proposal.
risks.impact: The project may optimize research comfort or produce an expensive audit record that cannot reconstruct the consequential decision.
risks.mitigation: Sell compliance or reduced incident-resolution time, retaining only necessary evidence.
risks.mitigation_failure: Compliance usefulness is buyer- and jurisdiction-specific; redaction can remove replay inputs, and generated explanations are not authenticated observations.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Neither a richer provenance graph nor claimed compliance establishes demand or permission to retain data.
risks.kill_scope: A product sold primarily on incremental provenance value in the chosen buyer segment.
risks.rejection_condition: Native logs meet actual audit/debugging needs at lower cost, and target buyers decline a funded pilot for the incremental capability after seeing its measured outcomes and price.

risks.title: Portability lacks aligned distribution incentives
risks.critique: Providers and incumbent tool vendors may gain more from integrated workflows than from maintaining a neutral compatibility contract, while buyers may purchase support and outcomes rather than portability.
risks.evidence_limit: Terraform's license conditions demonstrate that reusable ecosystem access has commercial boundaries; they do not establish any vendor's intentions toward MEDP or predict adoption.
risks.impact: The portable layer may lack distribution, lawful access to required components, sustainable funding or a distinct payer.
risks.mitigation: Use open governance, permissive components and paid certification/support.
risks.mitigation_failure: Support and certification recreate ongoing costs and incumbent advantages; a license does not supply maintainers, customers or agreement.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: Commercial incentives and contract rights cannot be standardized into existence.
risks.kill_scope: A broadly adopted neutral ecosystem or defensible standalone vendor position.
risks.rejection_condition: The target workflow lacks a feasible licensing/distribution route or neither integrators nor buyers will fund the shared layer at its cost-covering price.

risks.title: The thesis can retreat until no result refutes it
risks.critique: Encode only when worthwhile is a decision rule, not evidence of an opportunity; compatible clients agree can become true by excluding every disagreeing client after testing.
risks.evidence_limit: This is a methodological critique of the current claim wording, not evidence that a bounded useful implementation cannot exist.
risks.impact: The demonstrator can confirm an architecture by construction while leaving economics, portability and product value untested.
risks.mitigation: Freeze a workload, compatibility profile, buyer hypothesis, horizon and rejection rules before implementation.
risks.mitigation_failure: Changing scope after seeing results without recording rejection makes the mitigation circular; merely adding a falsifiability field changes nothing.
risks.architecture_cannot_resolve: No architecture can falsify an unrestricted existential claim using a finite negative case.
risks.kill_scope: The current thesis as an empirically testable product claim if ex-ante commitments are refused; not all possible future niches.
risks.rejection_condition: The team cannot state a result it would accept as rejection, or responds to a failed preregistered test only by redefining supported domains or clients.

experiments.title: All-in cost against credible native baselines
experiments.design: Preregister a platform-team buyer hypothesis, .NET 6 to .NET 10 workload, six-month horizon and buyer-confirmed reuse volume. Start with 12 independently selected repositories and three hosting profiles as a feasibility pilot. Compare expert/native tooling, native tooling plus a model, shared-package tooling plus the same model, and project-local scripts plus that model. Use isolated teams, blocked random assignment and blinded acceptance review; record failed and abandoned work.
experiments.controls: Same compiler, analyzers, native transforms, external checks, task inputs, permissions and safety requirements. Freeze model/tool versions for each comparison. Meter labor and compute separately; prevent solution leakage between arms. Prespecify sample size and repository-clustered uncertainty for any confirmatory study; the small pilot does not estimate rare-loss rates.
measurements: safety failures and declared tail-loss scenarios
experiments.reject: Reject the bounded economic claim if even optimistic credible six-month incremental savings versus the best qualifying baseline are nonpositive. Safety failures independently reject release. A suggested commercial continuation gate is at least 20 percent full-cost savings with noninferior acceptance quality, agreed before running, not a measured result.
experiments.inconclusive: Intervals straddle break-even, buyer volume is unknown, quality is not comparable, or maintenance/loss assumptions dominate. Do not promote a pilot or sensitivity projection to measured ROI.

experiments.title: Independent-client and target-observation challenge
experiments.design: Freeze supported observations, semantics, engine dependencies and outputs before a second team integrates the package into a second client. Include preserve-hosting, Azure Container Apps and AWS ECS profiles; missing input, unsupported version and denial cases; and a separate messaging stress case drawn from documented delivery/deduplication distinctions.
experiments.controls: Both clients may use the same declared native engines. Two transports calling one already-integrated facade do not establish independent integration. No post-hoc compatibility exclusions or shared client-specific rule forks. Messaging stress results do not automatically refute the narrower hosting prototype.
experiments.reject: One supported disagreement, silently invented missing fact or required neutral-core provider rule rejects the declared portability profile. Measured extra observation requirements reject scan-once for that workload, not all neutral facts.
experiments.inconclusive: Only happy paths or one shared integration are exercised, or no independent expected outcomes exist.

experiments.title: Independent oracle and authority failure injection
experiments.design: In disposable fixtures seed a semantically wrong but well-formed rule, inconsistent hard policies, stale observations, a false success report, an omitted behavioral invariant and a bypass attempt outside the approved executor. Include an authenticated test package with deliberately incorrect semantics; do not use actual malicious software.
experiments.controls: Independent reviewer defines invariants before package authors see cases. Tests run without production credentials. State the trusted computing base, adversary permissions and required audit/override behavior. Compare native CI/approval gates with the package gate under identical privileges.
experiments.reject: Any in-scope denied action executed without authorized override, or a damaging seeded action accepted under supposedly sufficient checks, rejects the corresponding authority/safety guarantee.
experiments.inconclusive: A simulation with no real privilege boundary only tests decision logic. Zero seeded failures does not establish a production incident rate or general semantic correctness.

experiments.title: Two update cycles and maintainer handoff
experiments.design: Replay two pinned historical upstream changes, then transfer maintenance to someone other than the author. Include engine skew, changed provider constraint, policy exception, unavailable dependency and test-package revocation. Run the same changes through the native and project-local baselines.
experiments.controls: Freeze update time budget, supported profiles, revocation deadline and review requirements before testing. Separate replayed historical work and projected future maintenance from live observed costs. Apply model improvements to all relevant arms, including package authorship.
experiments.reject: A declared-supported update silently fails or accepts revoked content beyond its deadline. Reject the bounded maintenance economics if measured costs eliminate the E01 savings at the declared volume.
experiments.inconclusive: No independent maintainer, cherry-picked easy releases, unpriced support or unsupported future cost extrapolation.

experiments.title: Buyer and provenance ablation
experiments.design: Recruit five independently budget-owning platform teams as a discovery sample, not a market estimate. Compare the same accepted migration with ordinary native CI/decision logs versus added rule-level lineage, then test a second-client integration task. Hide product labels during outcome evaluation. Measure incident reconstruction and audit acceptance, then offer a transparently costed funded pilot.
experiments.controls: Same migration, reviewer access and retention/privacy limits; measure provenance maintenance and redaction overhead. Verify actual audit requirements with the buyer rather than claiming generic compliance. Record objections, nonresponses and licensing/distribution blockers without inventing willingness to pay.
measurements: time to reconstruct a wrong decision
experiments.reject: For the sampled segment, stop a provenance-led product if native records suffice and no team funds the measured incremental capability at a cost-covering price. If only managed execution/support sells, reject package format as the primary value proposition and record the narrower service result.
experiments.inconclusive: Praise, hypothetical willingness, non-budget-holders, recruitment failure or five interviews alone do not establish market-wide absence of demand.
